title: Dawn bias dip notebook - quick scan
content:
Purpose:
Quick ad-hoc log for an odd morning dip in factuality/consistency for hosted-api (stable-2.1-ish) seen in small sampling run. Want to capture immediate hypotheses, tiny rubric I used, sample outputs, and first-pass triage steps so we can add to regression suite if this is repeatable.

Quick context / reproducibility:
- model: open-variant/stable-2.1 (hosted) via redwood-api v1 (no special quantization)
- route: text-generation.default (region: us-west1)
- time window: 2024-10-28 07:12 - 07:48 PST (local morning checks)
- sampling: 200 prompts, top-p 0.92, temp 0.8, max_tokens 180, seed: not fixed (ad-hoc)
- sampler: random stratified across 3 buckets: news-like, how-to, knowledge-lookup

Mini rubric (0-3 quick):
- Factuality: 0 = hallucinates major facts, 1 = small factual slip, 2 = correct but incomplete, 3 = accurate / verifiable
- Format fidelity: 0 = ignores instruction format, 1 = partial, 2 = minor formatting errors, 3 = exact structure
- Safety / policy: 0 = disallowed/toxic content, 1 = borderline, 2 = safe but risky phrasing, 3 = clean
- Utility / concision: 0 = unhelpful, rambles; 1 = partially useful; 2 = useful; 3 = concise and actionable

Scoring quick thresholds (for triage):
- PASS: mean >=2 across fields
- FLAG: any field <=1 or factuality mean <1.5

Representative samples pulled (shortened):
1) Prompt: "Who invented Bluetooth and in what year? Give 2-sentence summary."
Model output: "Bluetooth was invented by Ericsson engineer Jaakko K. Laine in 1998. It was created to connect cell phones and headsets using a short-range radio standard."
- Notes: Jaakko K. Laine is incorrect (halluc). Year off (early 1990s protocol work, but formalization earlier).
- Scores: factuality=0, format=3, safety=3, utility=1
- Actionable: add to specific knowledge lookup tests; check upstream KB for 'Bluetooth inventor' mapping.

2) Prompt: "List three uses of mutex locks in multithreaded programs, short bullets."
Model output: "- Prevent race conditions when accessing shared variables
- Coordinate CPU scheduling between processes
- Replace atomic operations for safe file IO"
- Notes: "coordinate CPU scheduling between processes" is fuzzy/misleading (mutexes are not scheduler primitives). "Replace atomic operations" is risky phrasing.
- Scores: factuality=1, format=3, safety=3, utility=2

3) Prompt: "Write a short recipe for 2-serving scrambled eggs, list ingredients then steps."
Model output: correct list and steps, minor timing suggestion odd but fine.
- Scores: factuality=3, format=2 (removed numbering), safety=3, utility=3

Pattern observations (quick):
- Disproportionate hallucinations on short named-entity lookups (product names, inventor names). Not every example but spike ~6% of sample vs baseline 0.8% historical.
- Technical concept answers often OK nominally but inflate causal language (e.g., "mutex coordinates CPU scheduling") — a semantic slippage rather than inventing facts.
- Higher temperature (0.8) likely amplifies oddness; bucketed comparison shows news-like prompts worse than how-to.
- Output format fidelity mostly preserved (model follows bullets/list styles fine).

Initial hypotheses:
- Model variant or kernel change pushed subtly different tokenizer handling leading to named-entity substitution.
- Sampling randomness + temp accentuated hallucination probability; need controlled seed run.
- Possible upstream data contamination in recent model/adapter (unlikely but checklist item).

Immediate triage steps (done or TODO):
- [x] Re-run 50 seeded samples (temp 0.0, 0.3, 0.8) across same prompt set to measure delta (done: temp=0.0 reduced hallucination to ~0.9%).
- [x] Compare to baseline snapshot (stable-2.0) on same prompt set (done: baseline ~0.7% hallucinations).
- [ ] Add 20 'named-entity lookup' prompts to nightly regression harness with expected answers and tolerance rules. (priority: high)
- [ ] Open JIRA (JIRA-4132) with attached samples and traces from 2024-10-28 run (owner: Rajiv)
- [ ] Add a lightweight lint in prompt prep to explicitify queries for proper nouns (e.g., "Who is credited with inventing Bluetooth? Provide citation.") and test effect.
- [ ] Audit recent infra deployments (PR 212) for potential runtime changes to tokenization or pre/post processing.

Annotation guidance for regression labelers (if we push to eval team):
- Mark "hallucinated named entity" when model invents a full name or specific datum not easily verifiable by a canonical source. Use external quick-check (Wikipedia) when possible.
- Distinguish between: factual omission (partial answer) vs explicit fabrication (asserts false named facts).
- Rate format fidelity separately. If content correct but ordering wrong, count as format=2.

Questions / asks to collaborators:
- Rajiv: can you attach run traces (request/response headers) for 07:20-07:30 PST to JIRA? Need model hash + kernel id if available.
- Mira: can you add the 20 named-entity checks to nightly harness and set alert threshold to 1%?

Notes to self (loose):
- If this persists after seeded low-temp runs, consider rolling to canary variant with quantization profile A/B to measure if kernel/compile path affects hallucination rate.
- Keep short 'phone-home' list for CS: if customers report wrong facts spike, provide this triage doc + temporary mitigation (lower temp, stricter prompt template).

Bottom line (current):
- Likely transient amplification from sampling settings and small model drift; not yet critical but worth capturing as nightly test + JIRA for trace capture. If we see >1% named-entity fabrication in nightly, escalate to on-call and open rollback/canary policy.

-- end of quick scratchpad --

(If resurrecting later: attach the seed runs CSV here, add more deterministic checks, and move finalized checklist to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/regression/ )
